FILE: research/audits/api_inputs/2026-11-13-balanced-witt/height-construction.md
Construct ONE missing native height compiler, or exhibit an exact falsifier. For an arbitrary expanded TOTALLY IMAGINARY number field K of growing degree N and a nonsingular form of rank at most8, give a polynomial-BIT quantum-under-GRH full Witt reduction whose expanded coefficients and change-of-basis satisfy H_out <= C H_in + P(field), for ABSOLUTE C independent of N. H=N times absolute logarithmic Weil height, summed over constant-size tuples. All unit/norm backend inputs must be expanded. Existing norm residue postprocessor provides a first expanded fractional norm witness; existing conic C1/C2 shortening provides absolute height slope for a known expanded conic witness. Tower-only square-root calls can be replaced by Lenstra root factoring over K. The main NEW difficulty is q4 descent and q5 local CRT selection with affine slope: consider a short gamma in ideal I and reduce CRT representatives modulo gamma O_K subset I; no huge primitive-generator advice. Pay local representatives, integral or fractional normalization, auxiliary discriminants, all coordinate maps and absolute slope. Ordinary polynomial output in H is insufficient. We need a construction independent of old witness height, not an existence theorem or repetition of an ACCEPT label. Try to disprove degree-independent slope first. Do not construct the whole growing-rank balanced tree; the other obligation covers that. State exact hypotheses, proof, numerical generous C if possible, and the first unpaid operation if no closure. No code, no citations you cannot distinguish as unverified, no infrastructure.

# Balanced expanded Witt decomposition

2026-11-13. New candidate, NOT admitted. Start STATE/TRAPS, then corpus
been-tried/baselines for balanced Witt decomposition and actual primary
sources. The previous ternary INTEGRAL-isometry seed remains open; this is
a different native output over a field, not a claim that its gate disappeared.

## Problem, mechanism, and reason to test it

Native input: a totally imaginary number field K of growing degree N,
explicit compatible defining polynomial/maximal-order basis/table, and a
nonsingular symmetric d-by-d matrix Q over K, expanded binary coordinates.
Output a FULL EXPANDED basis W with W^T Q W equal to a sum of canonical
hyperbolic planes and an anisotropic form of rank <=4. Both N,d grow. A
subsequent exact rational isometry of two such forms is a possible endpoint;
integral isometry, real-field extension, short lattice witnesses, novelty,
hardness, implementation and quantum execution are not claimed.

Target quantum polynomial(native bits,log(1/eta)) BIT/gates/output under
the explicit GRH of the admitted scalar norm backend. The expected benefit
is replacing the same classical class/unit/norm arithmetic by known quantum
arithmetic. No proven classical lower bound or asymptotic separation follows.
Supplied quadratic towers retain the stronger existing ERH factoring baseline.

The new norm-residue operation first upgrades the existing single-five-plane
isotropic-vector construction to expanded output: only one constant-rank
quaternion splitting and its fixed-size descent follow the expanded front end.
This is a direct consequence, not a reason to spend another paid confirmation.
The NEW operation to test is height-controlled composition of many such calls.

Diagonalize once. Each leaf is a one-dimensional form. At each node merge
the two surviving anisotropic cores, of total rank <=8, and split off all
hyperbolic planes. Carry only the new core of rank <=4. A balanced tree has
depth ceil(log2 d). The bound on anisotropic rank uses the totally imaginary
number-field Hasse principle and finite u-invariant4; it fails over real fields.

The decisive unproved lemma is a native fixed-rank <=8 reduction whose
coefficients AND change-of-basis have extensive absolute height

    H_out <= C H_in + P(charged field data),

with an ABSOLUTE constant C, independent of N,d and coefficient heights.
Here H_K(x)=N h(x), summed only over bounded-rank tuples. A factor N in C
would leave N^O(log d), and a nonlinear power of H would be worse. Neither
is acceptable. The expanded norm solver alone guarantees only a polynomial
output bound and does not prove this affine lemma.

Candidate height repair: the reviewed C1 ideal reset/C2 weighted squareclass
compression gives absolute-slope conic shortening of an ALREADY EXPANDED
witness. Its former tower root extraction can now be replaced by actual
Lenstra polynomial factoring over the original K. For q5 local gluing, take
a short nonzero gamma in the CRT ideal I by Minkowski LLL and reduce a CRT
representative modulo gamma*O_K, a SUBLATTICE of I. The basis gamma*omega_i
may yield a coefficient-height slope independent of N. These details, local
integrality, auxiliary discriminants and all fixed-rank maps need proof.

## Classical and source checks

Corpus returns existing compact isotropy, class/unit and LLL baselines;
lexical nonmatches are not novelty or hardness evidence. Actual primary
Fukshansky Theorem1.3 gives small-height Witt components by an existence
argument, starting with an existential maximal isotropic subspace. It does
not by itself supply this native polynomial compiler. Actual Koprowski–
Rothkegel assumes principal generators, S-class/S-unit computations and
Algorithm8 enlarges support until an F2 system solves. Its stated output is
an abstract anisotropic form, not a full embedded basis with this clock.
Retained PDFs/text/metadata: audits/sources/2026-11-13-balanced-witt/.
No exhaustive literature priority claim or claim their algorithms are slow.

Cheapest falsifiers: trace every height recurrence symbolically before any
quantum implementation; expose N-dependent slopes, nonlinear input-height
dependence, uncharged compact expansion, growing field towers, supplied
starting witnesses, unbounded support searches or basis reconstruction costs.
No backend or new research infrastructure is proposed. If the height lemma
fails, retain the single-vector corollary but do not promote full decomposition.

# Expanded norm witnesses and native ternary transport

2026-11-13. Reviewed WRITTEN global construction and local finite verifier;
full integral isometry is NOT admitted. The coupled dyadic seed is still open. Start STATE/TRAPS after the closed native
metabelian pass. Corpus been-tried/baselines for compact norm parity and
ternary spinor transport were checked before literature. Catalogue matches
were mostly lexical, not evidence of missing classical algorithms.

## Selection and native contract

Independent comparison excluded wild-local Kummer conditioning: later
LOCAL_KUMMER_ALL_PRIMES.md and GENERAL_NATIVE_SELMER_COMPOSITION.md already
close that written endpoint, superseding old OPEN rows. Conductivity still
lacks a new cancellation-preserving classical contraction. The present
route has a concrete new operation: decompactify an exact fractional norm
witness by exponent residues and one root in the BASE field. This may
remove the specific global support blocker in the retained ternary route.

Native input: arbitrary expanded totally real number fieldK with maximal
order tables, and two nonsingular integral ternary Gram matrices A,B,
indefinite at a real place. Output integral-isometry DECISION, failureeta,
target quantum poly(nativebits,log1eta) under the explicit GRH used by
complete compact units/norms. No common ambient embedding, local transporter
spinor offset, class/unit basis, support or precision advice is supplied.
Mechanism: expanded global isometry via relative norms/quaternions, native
local integral transport/spinor offsets, complete spinor ray-class decision.
The SINGLE end-to-end question is whether these newly expanded global
objects and a paid local-offset compiler close the native decision route.

Strongest classical baseline is the SAME norm/class-unit/ray-class reduction,
plus existing local lattice algorithms. Over supplied quadratic towers, the
recent ERH factoring reduction is stronger and must be reused. No classical
lower bound, novelty, practicality or Shor-level claim follows. Hidden
number-field degree constants, enumerating p^precision residues, expanding
large binary powers, unproved local lifting, or supplied offsets are falsifiers.

## Elementary decompactification (parent derivation)

Let L/K have degree d, with charged expanded field tables/embedding, and
a!=0 inK expanded. Suppose a genuine POWER PRODUCT
 beta=prod_(i=1)^t b_i^(e_i),  N_L/K(beta)=a,
is supplied, where each b_i is a nonzero SMALL EXPANDED L-element and
e_i is a binary signed integer. This is the exact output contract of
RELATIVE_NORM_TENSOR_SUPPORT.md. Arbitrary arithmetic circuits are excluded.

Write e_i=d*q_i+r_i by Euclidean division, 0<=r_i<d, and compute
 beta0=prod b_i^(r_i) in expanded coordinates. With gamma=prod b_i^(q_i),
 beta=beta0*gamma^d, so c=N(beta0)/a=N(gamma)^(-d) is a dth power IN K.
Factor X^d-c overK, choose ANY linear-factor rootz, and return beta0/z.
Its norm is N(beta0)/z^d=a. Neither gamma nor the original huge beta is
evaluated. For d=1 return the embedded a directly. Negative exponents use
Euclidean residues; no sign convention is implicit.

The total number of factors with multiplicity is <=t(d-1), polynomial
because d<=[L:Q] is an expanded dimension. Product coordinate height is
polynomial in the atom/table bit lengths, t and d. Norm by determinant,
X^d-c, number-field factorization and the output all have polynomial BIT
size. Base-field root extraction, not a splitting field, is required.
This proves a deterministic polynomial postprocessor conditional on the
standard explicit number-field polynomial-factorization interface. The
actual A.K.Lenstra1982 source encoding and final theorem are being checked.

It preserves EXACT FRACTIONAL norm. It does NOT preserve integrality,
S-unit support, archimedean constraints, a chosen projective point or the
original element. Pell integral-witness bounds therefore do not contradict
it. No extension to a general compact sum/circuit or coupled norm system
is asserted. With the existing complete GRH norm backend it gives a
polynomial EXPANDED output, not merely a compact one, for this contract.

## Proposed explicit quaternion and common-space construction

Quaternion inputs are A=(c,d0), B=(a0,b) overK. Determine split/isomorphic
status through the already charged local Hilbert-symbol/ramification tests.
All following calls have EXPANDED targets and field degree at most4[K:Q].
Compute auxiliary maximal orders using the retained discriminant-radical
Buchmann-Lenstra interface; do not supply them as advice.

For B split, if a0 is nonsquare, solve N_K(sqrt(a0))/K(x+y sqrt(a0))=b
with the compact backend and the residue postprocessor. Matrices
 i=[[0,a0],[1,0]], j=[[x,-a0*y],[y,-x]]
give an explicit expanded split representation. A square a0 has a direct
representation. Split A and B are then matched via M2(K).

For the common DIVISION case, c is nonsquare. Let E=K(sqrt(c)). If a0
is square inE, K(sqrt(a0))=E: a base root of a0/c gives x inB withx²=c.
Otherwise solve the quadratic norm equation overE that splits B_E.
For z in E(sqrt(a0)) with normb, q=z+j is a nonzero reduced-norm-zero
element of B_E. Write q=u+v sqrt(c), u,v inB. Division ofB impliesv!=0
and Nrd(v)!=0. Its norm identity gives
 Nrd(u)+c*Nrd(v)=0, u*bar(v)+v*bar(u)=0.
Thus x=u*v^(-1) has trace0, norm-c and squarec. Everything is expanded.

Choose any nonzero y0 in the two-dimensional linear anticommuter ofx.
SinceB is division, t=y0² lies inK*; solve N_E/K(w)=d0/t. The isomorphism
assumption guarantees solubility by the standard common-quadratic-subfield
classification. Put y=w(x)*y0. Then x²=c,y²=d0,xy=-yx. Their four basis
images give the expanded algebra isomorphism. All inverses/pivots/norms
have polynomial expanded bit size, so prime support is now factorable.

For diagonal ternaries, v -> volume_element*v identifies each vector
space with the pure even Clifford algebra, with norm det(Gram)*q(v).
An even-Clifford isomorphism plus a square root of detA/detB therefore
gives a rational isometry after scalar correction. Fixed-rank diagonal
changes and all root tests are charged. Factor expanded coordinate
numerators/denominators and the determinant to obtain a polynomial-size
exceptional set outside which the map and its inverse are integral.
This is under independent review, not inferred from Magma documentation.


FILE: research/audits/api_inputs/2026-11-13-balanced-witt/conic-shortening.md
# Native tower witness shortening — independent proof, 2026-11-13

**Accepted at the stated expanded-input/factoring scope.** An ALREADY GIVEN
nonzero ternary witness over an original quadratic-tower field can be replaced
by one whose extensive absolute height has an ABSOLUTE constant slope in the
coefficient heights. The output bound is independent of the old witness height.
This proves the postprocessing lemma in section 3 of the terminal batched-
compiler report. It does not discover a first witness or, by itself, prove the
report's full coupled tower schedule.

The entire terminal 689-LF report was read, together with STATE/TRAPS and the
stable reset proofs. The maximal-order import was checked against the actual
Buchmann--Lenstra primary theorem, proof and uniform encoding sections. No API,
network, Git, new implementation, numerical sweep or mutable report was used.

## 1. Input, output and normalization

Let K be an ORIGINAL supplied quadratic-tower field of degree n=2^i, with
maximal-order integral basis, exact field/tower conversions, and discriminant
Delta_K=abs(disc K). Every encoded bit is charged. Use natural logarithms and
  H_K(u)=n*h(u),
where h is the absolute logarithmic Weil height. Set H_K(0)=0 and sum this
height over fixed-rank tuples. In particular, the finite contribution is
  sum_P max(0,-v_P(u))*log N(P).
Complex archimedean embeddings are counted twice.

For a diagonal nonsingular ternary
  A*x^2+B*y^2+C*z^2=0,  A*B*C!=0,
put d=-B/A, a=-C/A, and H_coeff=H_K(A)+H_K(B)+H_K(C). Then
  x^2-d*y^2=a*z^2,                 H_K(a)+H_K(d)<=2*H_coeff.  (1)
The algorithm takes an EXPANDED nonzero witness of this equation as input.
It returns an expanded rational K-coordinate witness satisfying
  H_K(x0)+H_K(y0)+H_K(z0)
     <=64*(H_coeff+log Delta_K+n^2).                         (2)
Its runtime is polynomial in the CURRENT expanded field/coefficient/witness
input, with integer factoring and certified finite-field factoring charged.

The square test and root extraction over ORIGINAL K are already constructive:
section 6 of `2026-11-13-tagged-tower-conditional-composition.md` gives at most
3^i<=n^2 calls on the supplied tower, including polynomial-size arguments.
The rational leaf uses integer-square tests. This is not a new conic oracle.
If d=s^2, a binary zero (s,1,0) suffices. If a norm witness with z!=0 is needed,
use ((a+1)/2,(a-1)/(2s),1); it obeys the same bound. Hence assume d nonsquare.

Set L=K(t), t^2=d, so [L:Q]=2n. The old witness must have z!=0, since otherwise
d would be a square (or the witness would vanish). Thus
  beta=(x+y*t)/z !=0,                   N_(L/K)(beta)=a.      (3)
The auxiliary extension will only be used for explicit arithmetic and LLL,
never for a recursive U, conic, isotropy or class-group computation.

## 2. A native auxiliary order with the RIGHT discriminant bound

Factor the principal FRACTIONAL ideal (d), including denominator primes, and
form
  D_d=product_P P^floor(v_P(d)/2),
  J_d=(d)*D_d^(-2)=product_P P^(v_P(d) mod 2).                (4)
The remainder is in {0,1}, including for negative valuations. Thus J_d is
integral squarefree, while D_d can be fractional and nonprincipal.

The preferred initial order is the actual Z-lattice
  A_L=O_K direct-sum (D_d^(-1)*t) inside L.                  (5)
It contains 1 and is closed under multiplication, since
  d*D_d^(-2)=J_d subset O_K.
It is therefore an order of absolute rank 2n. This does NOT suppose that
D_d is principal or that O_L has a free relative integral basis over O_K.
Use the given Z-basis omega_1,...,omega_n of O_K and an HNF-derived Z-basis
eta_1,...,eta_n of D_d^(-1), giving the explicit basis (omega_i,eta_i*t).

The trace matrix is block diagonal: its even block is 2*Tr_K(omega_i*omega_j),
its odd block is 2*Tr_K(d*eta_i*eta_j), and its mixed blocks vanish. Changing
the ideal basis from omega to eta has absolute determinant N(D_d)^(-1).
Taking determinants gives the EXACT absolute discriminant
  abs(disc A_L)=4^n*Delta_K^2*abs(N_(K/Q)d)*N(D_d)^(-2)
              =4^n*Delta_K^2*N(J_d).                       (6)
Since disc(A_L)=disc(O_L)*[O_L:A_L]^2,
  log Delta_L<=2*log Delta_K+2n*log 2+log N(J_d)
              <=2*log Delta_K+2n*log 2+2*H_K(d).             (7)
For the last inequality, each of the positive and negative valuation masses
is at most H_K(d), by the product formula. In particular their sum is at most
2H_K(d); the odd support is bounded by that sum. This elementary order proof
is stronger than the report's 3n*log 2 version and needs no local different
formula or uncharged discriminant oracle.

Everything in (4)--(6) is constructible with polynomial bits in the expanded
input. To find principal-ideal support, choose c with c*d integral and factor
c*abs(N(c*d)); using N(d) alone would miss split numerator/denominator
cancellations. Decompose the factored primes in O_K and compute valuations.
The valuation integers have polynomial numerical size in the expanded input
length; the rational primes have polynomial BIT length, not bounded magnitude. Ideal
products/inverses and integer HNF construct D_d and its inverse. Exact field
arithmetic gives the INTEGRAL multiplication constants of the basis in (5).
No ideal is principalized.

Factor abs(disc A_L), whose bit length is bounded by (7), and use its FULL
radical, retaining primes of EVEN discriminant exponent. The actual
Buchmann--Lenstra 1994 Theorem 1.2 and proof of Theorem 1.3 compute O_L in
polynomial BIT time from this order and radical. Their order representation
uses the degree and n^3 integer structure constants; section 5.9 bounds every
overorder encoding and Theorem 6.7 pays the uniform clock. The stable source
review `2026-11-13-maximal-order-source-check.md` supplies the precise import.
I additionally read actual LF249--281, 1312--1365, 1607--1642, 1720--1730 and
1763--1778 in the retained primary text; physical LF locators are used.

Consequently a maximal-order basis of L, its multiplication table and exact
conversions to K+K*t are computed, not supplied as advice. Certified embeddings
and rational-Gram LLL use the already paid root/metric compiler in the weighted
reset proof. Their intermediate encodings can contain polynomial degree factors.
They are temporary workspace; the HEIGHT bound below uses (7), not a possibly
large monogenic discriminant or the auxiliary basis condition number.

## 3. Remove incoming witness support without finding another witness

Let S* consist of all dyadic K-primes and every numerator/denominator prime of
a and d. This set depends ONLY on the coefficients. Its mass satisfies
  w*=sum_(P in S*) log N(P)<=n*log 2+2H_K(a)+2H_K(d).         (8)
Outside S*, d is a unit and 2 is invertible, so L/K is unramified or split.
The norm identity (3) implies that the parity divisor of beta is pulled back
from a squarefree base ideal R outside S*: at a split prime the two valuations
have even sum and hence equal parity; at an inert prime there is one parity.
Here a is actually a unit outside S*, so the inert valuation is zero, though
this stronger observation is unnecessary.

Construct R by factoring the expanded principal fractional ideal of beta and
recording these parities. All numerator/denominator work is charged to the OLD
witness input length. Apply the independently proved generic ideal reset C1:
  choose w in R^(-1), M=(w)*R integral, with
  N(M)<=3^(n/2)*2^(n(n-1)/4)*sqrt(Delta_K).                  (9)
Its rational Minkowski-Gram computation and recorded LLL vector are polynomial
in the expanded input. It computes neither a class group nor a unit basis.
Outside S*, parity(w*beta) is now the pullback of odd(M), while
  N_(L/K)(w*beta)=a*w^2.                                    (10)

Apply weighted squareclass compression C2 IN L to w*beta. It constructs
  beta0=w*beta*gamma^2 in O_L, beta0!=0.                     (11)
C2 preserves the upper squareclass of w*beta. C1 generally changes the upper
squareclass of beta, which is allowed when replacing a ternary witness.
It preserves the lower norm squareclass, as required in (10).

Let J be the squarefree odd ideal of beta0. At an exceptional base prime P,
the sum of residue degrees of upper primes is at most 2. Outside S*, pullback
has ramification index one and its ideal norm is the square of the base norm.
It follows that
  log N_L(J)<=2*w*+2*log N_K(M).                             (12)
This bound is independent of the old witness height. C2 can introduce new EVEN
valuations elsewhere; these do not enlarge J and must not be mistaken for
new odd support. The dyadic primes were explicitly included in S*.

## 4. Explicit constant-slope output height

For an extension of absolute degree 2n, the proved C2 bound is
  max_sigma |sigma(beta0)|
    <=3*2^((2n-1)/2)*(Delta_L*N_L(J))^(1/(2n)).              (13)
Integrality removes every finite contribution to its height. Combining
(7)--(9), (12), and (13) gives, writing Ha=H_K(a), Hd=H_K(d),
  H_L(beta0)
    <=2n*log 3+n*(2n-1)*log 2+log Delta_L+log N_L(J)
    <=4Ha+6Hd+3*log Delta_K
       +3n*log 3+(5/2)*n*(n+1)*log 2
    <=4Ha+6Hd+3*log Delta_K+7n^2.                           (14)
The last inequality is valid even for n=1. This displays the ABSOLUTE slope;
there is no multiplying degree or coefficient-dependent polynomial in it.

The known involution tau(t)=-t gives
  x0=(beta0+tau(beta0))/2,
  y0=(beta0-tau(beta0))/(2*t).                              (15)
These elements lie in K and are computed by the exact K+K*t conversion.
Furthermore N(beta0)/a is a nonzero square in K, since by (3) and (11)
  N(beta0)/a=(w*N_(L/K)(gamma))^2.                          (16)
One may retain gamma and use w*N(gamma), or use the paid exact root routine
on ORIGINAL K. In either case take z0 with z0^2=N(beta0)/a. Then
  x0^2-d*y0^2=a*z0^2, z0!=0.
There is no search for a new conic point in this extraction.

The standard absolute-height sum/product inequalities, h(1/2)=log 2,
h(t)=h(d)/2, H_L(u)=2H_K(u) for u in K, and conjugacy invariance give
  H_K(x0)<=H_L(beta0)+2n*log 2,
  H_K(y0)<=H_L(beta0)+2n*log 2+Hd/2,
  H_K(z0)<=H_L(beta0)/2+Ha/2.                              (17)
For the last line, H_K(N beta0)<=H_L(beta0) and h(z0^2)=2h(z0).
Thus their sum is at most
  (5/2)*H_L(beta0)+(Ha+Hd)/2+4n*log 2
    <=32*(Ha+Hd+log Delta_K+n^2).                          (18)
Equation (1) proves (2). If an EXACT relative norm-a element is requested,
return (x0+y0*t)/z0; inversion adds another absolute height factor only.

A general nonsingular rank-three form can first be diagonalized by a constant
number of field operations and 3-by-3 solves. Every nonzero pivot and the
inverse coordinate change have height bounded by an absolute constant times
the original fixed-rank coefficient heights plus O(n). This yields the same
form of conclusion with another absolute constant. Formula (2) itself is
asserted for the diagonal ternaries actually used by the native recurrence.

## 5. Finite expanded coordinates, and the limits of this lemma

For the ORIGINAL supplied integral basis of K, the maximum numerator or
denominator bit height of an element u satisfies
  ell_K(u)<=2*H_K(u)/log 2+kappa_K+O(1),                    (19)
where kappa_K is polynomially bounded by the charged original field/basis
input. To see this, choose the least integer m>0 with m*u integral. Its log
is at most the denominator-ideal mass, hence at most H_K(u). Every embedding
of m*u has absolute value at most exp(2H_K(u)); trace-dual/cofactor bounds in
the fixed basis then bound all integer coordinates. This also handles a very
skew supplied basis. The TOTAL encoding has n such coordinates and can carry
an additional factor n. That runtime factor is not a propagated height slope.

The output must remain an expanded RATIONAL-coordinate vector. Unnecessarily
clearing all its denominators and then propagating that chosen integral vector
can add a degree factor to the affine tuple height; it is not part of (2).
Exact output conversion, norm computation, ideal factorization, maximal-order
setup, metric approximation and Gram-only LLL all cost polynomially many bits
in the incoming expanded input. The two stable reset proofs pay the finite
precision, LLL transformation coefficients and termination. No infinitesimal
embedding comparison, unknown condition number or free exact real operation
is being imported here. Integer factoring is still a charged resource.

The retained exact identities (11), (15), (16) and the conic equation certify
an accepted result. Probabilistic factorization routines may use their existing
bounded-clock/certified interface and an assigned failure budget. There is no
new dependence on a chosen numerical tolerance or the old witness's output
height beyond paying to READ and process that input.

Accepted: uniform constant-slope shortening of an existing expanded witness,
including rational K, complex auxiliary extensions, fractional coefficients,
nonprincipal D_d, growing degree and arbitrary charged integral bases. The
new vector need not preserve the old witness's projective point, prescribed
congruences or upper squareclass; those are not the isotropy interface here.
Neither C1 nor C2 can make an exponentially long ALREADY REQUIRED computation
of the incoming witness polynomial. A compact witness is not freely expanded.
The number/dependencies of conic/U batches and their joint original-input bit
bound remain a separate composition proof. No complete tower theorem,
implementation, novelty, hardness or quantum advantage is inferred here.

References used: the terminal `tower-batched-native-compiler/response.md`,
section 3; stable reviews `2026-11-13-squareclass-weighted-lll-compression.md`,
`2026-11-13-conic-content-support-normalization.md`,
`2026-11-13-tagged-tower-conditional-composition.md` section 6, and
`2026-11-13-maximal-order-source-check.md`; actual Buchmann--Lenstra primary
text under `audits/sources/2026-11-13-tower-native-composition/` at the LF
locators specified above. The LLL/metric proof remains the explicit rational-
Gram adaptation in the stable C1/C2 reviews, not an unqualified source import.

# Compact isotropy over arbitrary number fields

7 November 2026. Reviewed WRITTEN bounded-error quantum polynomial-BIT
isotropy decision and COMPACT isotropic-vector construction for every
explicit growing-degree number field and nondegenerate growing-dimension
form, under EXPLICIT GRH. Source/descent/local/composition reviews and one
focused classical/algebra control are complete. This is a deduction from
published arithmetic algorithms and the proofs below, not a human-reviewed
or formally verified theorem, implementation, novelty or speedup claim.
No algorithm is inferred from finite tests or AI acceptance labels.

## Native question and selection

Given a number field K of arbitrary charged degree n, a monic defining
polynomial, explicit maximal-order integral basis/multiplication table,
and an expanded nondegenerate symmetric d-by-d matrix Q over K, decide
isotropy and return a NONZERO isotropic vector if one exists. Both n and d
grow. The output is polynomial-size arithmetic circuits over the
supplied K basis, with a charged bounded-error classical verifier. Expanded,
short or integral points, repeated compact-input Witt decomposition, and
cryptographic short witnesses are different contracts and are not claimed.
Target: bounded-error quantum polynomial BIT time under EXPLICIT GRH.
No class group, unit basis, splitting, point, field closure or local root
is supplied as advice. Failure tolerance eta is charged logarithmically.

The mechanism reuses known quantum central-simple-algebra splitting
and supplies a paid small-dimensional descent and local-to-global reduction.
Its value is an explicit end-to-end arithmetic endpoint. Classical index
calculus/norm/S-unit methods and LLL remain competitors; factoring-oracle
algorithms already handle rational forms and special quadratic base fields.
Rational dimension >=5 has stronger algorithms avoiding factoring under GRH. No
classical hardness, separation or novelty follows from the general route.
